message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"aiuto","gloss":"aid, help","category":"means/aid","note":"Theuth's 'questo aiuto per la scienza e per la memoria' renders pharmakon as a neutral help; no medicinal or drug sense is kept."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"memoria","gloss":"memory","note":""},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"scienza","gloss":"knowledge, science","note":"Sophia is rendered 'scienza' here, but 'sapienti' and 'sapienza' are used elsewhere in the passage. Also the order is reversed: 'scienza' comes before 'memoria'."},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"mezzo","gloss":"means, medium","category":"means/aid","note":"The phrase is 'un mezzo di ritenere, ma di richiamare a memoria le cose'. The word differs from the 'aiuto' of 274e. A different word 'aiuto' also occurs in the same sentence, but it renders the 'external' help of written signs (ἔξωθεν), not pharmakon."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"ritenere","gloss":"to retain, to hold","note":"Rendered as a verb, 'a means of retaining', not as the noun 'memoria'. This loses the lexical echo of mneme with 274e."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"richiamare a memoria le cose","gloss":"to call things back to memory","note":"A verbal periphrasis for hypomnesis (reminding). It contains the word 'memoria', which blurs the contrast with mneme."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"una sapienza apparente e non la vera","gloss":"an apparent wisdom and not the true one","note":"Doxa is rendered as 'apparente' (apparent) and aletheia as 'la vera' (the true one), so the contrast is between apparent and true wisdom."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"avranno la sola apparenza","gloss":"they will have only the appearance","note":"The compound doxosophoi is dissolved into a clause: 'instead of being wise, they will have only the appearance (of wisdom)'. No single word corresponds to it."},"argument":"Dalbono does not keep one word for pharmakon: Theuth offers an 'aiuto' (help), while Thamus answers with a 'mezzo' (means) of recalling. The two words are near-synonyms but not identical, so Thamus does not turn Theuth's own word against him. The medicinal or poisonous ambiguity is entirely lost. The memory/reminding contrast is also blurred, since 'richiamare a memoria' contains the word 'memoria'."}
